_comment: P3 part-sourcer, LUM-DTR-STROBE-A (lumina-strobe), 2026-07-28. One entry per DISTINCT orderable part; refdes counts are in qty_per_board. Every row was re-verified live through parts_search at selection time (stock/price/datasheet URL as of this run). Build quantity 6; 'price' is the unit price at the price break that qty_per_board*6 reaches. Emitters, optics, the MCPCB, the heatsink, the two off-board leaded thermistors and the harness wire are NOT here: the light engine is specified, not designed, and is not bound to LCSC stock. MountingHole_3.2mm_M3 (H1-H5) and every TP are footprints, not purchased parts.

totals.extended_setup_fee_estimate: ~$3 per distinct Extended part per order = ~$78 over the run (~$13.00/board at 6)

revision: REV D, 2026-07-28. Rev B raised P3-OPEN-1 (a hot-swap fault timer cannot survive an 87 %-duty current-limit regime); rev C resourced the discrete linear limiter that replaced the controller after BLOCKING-04 accepted it. REV D does three things: fixes R2, which was announcing this board as the wrong daughter type; sources the rev-D comparator hysteresis network with the high-value resistors retargeted to the JLC Basic shelf where that is free; and promotes P3-OPEN-6 to a P10 cost item. Every changed part re-verified live.

correctness_fix: R2 ID_ADC bottom leg: 4.7k (C23162) -> 2.7k 1% (C13167). 4.7k is ICD-01 s3.4 CODE 2 = LUM-PAR-A; this board is CODE 1 = 2.7 kOhm. Left as-is the board would have announced itself to carrier firmware as the RGBW par and been handed the wrong daughter profile. 1 % is required, not 5 %: adjacent-code separation is 0.353 V against ~+/-0.05 V of worst-case divider error and a +/-0.15 V firmware detection window. CLOSES P3-OPEN-5.

C23219 620k 0603 x1 - U400D ceiling hysteresis, KEPT EXTENDED AND FLAGGED.

reuse_count_changed: C17514 1M 0805 1 -> 5. The four Vds-fault hysteresis resistors (~1 M, blocks.md s2.4.2) REUSE A LINE ALREADY ON THE BOM: zero new part number, zero value shift, zero feeder. This is the single biggest win of the retargeting exercise.

C25804 10k 0603 16 -> 27 (three reference-divider legs plus THE EIGHT 10 k PULL-UPS TO +12V, one per open-collector output - and R_pull sits inside the hysteresis divider, so it is part of the band arithmetic, not garnish).

C31850 22k 0603 8 -> 6 and C25819 47k 0603 8 -> 6 - the generic P4 estimate pool shrinks because ~20 previously-unpinned placements now have specified values.
delta_from_rev_c.rev_c_items_confirmed_present: Yes to all: LM2904BIDR is at 5 placements (U100 is the charge-loop error amp), 2N7002 carries the extra Q101 (and now Q404 as well, 16 total), Q100 is IRF5210STRLPBF P-channel, and the ballast (2 x 39R 2512), the two 12 V zeners and the 24k bias dropper are all present. LM5069, the 0.27R sense resistor and the PLIM 150k were deleted at rev C - note that the 150k LCSC code C22807 RETURNS at rev D for an unrelated reason (the LED-OT hysteresis).
delta_from_rev_c.cost: BOM $15.24 -> $15.60 per board at qty 6 (+$0.36, almost all of it the hysteresis network's placement count rather than its part cost). Distinct parts 40 -> 50; Basic 17 -> 24; Extended 23 -> 26. Placements 167 -> 194. Extended setup ~$69 -> ~$78 over the run (~$13/board). All-in with ~$3 PCB: ~$31.60/board.

hysteresis_retargeting_report.method: For each high-value resistor in blocks.md s2.4.2, checked JLC Basic availability at the specified value, then at the nearest E24 neighbours, in 0603 and 0805. Band effects recomputed from the architecture's own formula: band = R_ref x [(12 - V_ref)/(R_pull + R_hyst) + (V_ref - 0.25)/R_hyst], R_pull = 10k, V_OL = 0.25 V.

results.shift: 0 % - and NO NEW LINE AT ALL
results.verdict: BEST OUTCOME. This value was already on the BOM as the bleed-switch gate bias, so four placements were absorbed into an existing line. Reuse beat E24-neighbour hunting here, exactly as predicted.
TAKEN. The specified value is already on the Basic shelf; band stays 379 mV = 5.2 C of solder point, 25x Vio.

TAKEN. 560k is not Basic in any size. Physically this is 5.0 C -> 5.4 C of tab hysteresis and Vio margin 12x -> 12.8x. It is a slow thermal trip with the largest margin of the four sections and the shift is in the safe direction (more chatter immunity), so 0.4 C changes nothing operationally. Saves one Extended feeder.

FLAGGED, NOT TAKEN. There is no Basic E24 neighbour at all - 750k, 820k and 910k are absent from the Basic shelf in both 0603 and 0805. The only nearby Basic value is 1M (+22 %), which would shrink the band 58.7 -> 48.2 mV (-17.9 %) = 1.02 V -> 0.84 V of bank, and move Vio margin 3.9x -> 3.2x. blocks.md s2.4.2 judgement call 1 states the UVLO is ALREADY the tightest band on the board and is deliberately not widened, so spending a further 18 % of it to save ~$3 of setup is the architect's call, not P3's.

FLAGGED, NOT TAKEN. Again no Basic E24 neighbour (560k, 680k, 750k all absent from the Basic shelf). Nearest Basic is 510k, -17.7 % resistance, which WIDENS the band 81.9 -> 99.3 mV (+21.3 %) = 1.42 V -> 1.73 V of bank. That is a 0.31 V bite out of the 8.3 V operating window on the ceiling comparator specifically, so unlike the board-OT shift it is not free.

hysteresis_retargeting_report.net: Of the five high-value positions, three cost no Extended line at all (one by reuse, one exact-Basic, one retargeted) and two are flagged for the architect. Extended lines added by the hysteresis network: 2, against 3 if every specified value had been taken as-is. If the architect accepts both flagged moves, the network costs ZERO Extended lines.

extended_reduction_options.option: see hysteresis_retargeting_report - 1M and 510k respectively are the only Basic options and both move a band materially. Architect's call.
extended_reduction_options.saves: up to two Extended part numbers (~$6 setup, ~$1.00/board at qty 6)
extended_reduction_options.decision_owner: architect - these are hysteresis bands, not sourcing choices

Rth goes 9.43k -> 9.52k, still inside the ICD's 10k ADC limit; the bank and Vds dividers stay identical to each other so the Vds trip stays ratiometric. Cost: ADC0 full scale falls from 3.28 V to 2.71 V at 57 V, i.e. ~17 % less resolution on the bank telemetry.
extended_reduction_options.saves: one distinct Extended part number (~$3 setup, ~$0.50/board at qty 6)

deviations_from_architecture: R450 = 510k rather than the specified 560k - retargeted to the Basic shelf at +9.6 % band. See hysteresis_retargeting_report.

Q100 = IRF5210STRLPBF rather than a named MPN - blocks.md s2.2 rev C specifies only 'P-channel MOSFET, 100-150 V, D2PAK/DPAK'. Selected on die area at equal price: RthJC 0.75 vs 1.1 C/W and PD 170 vs 110 W against the IRF9540NS, with 3.7x the stock. See P3-OPEN-7.
U201..U351: SN74LVC1G3157DCKR (UMW) replaces the SGM3157 the architecture named; the temperature rationale is corrected in P3-OPEN-9 and the exception now clears against ICD s7.7.
U420: MCP23008T-E/SS replaces the PCF8574 / TCA9534 class; rationale corrected in P3-OPEN-8 and the exception now clears against ICD s7.7.
Q200..Q350: the four pass FETs remain one IRF640NSTRLPBF part number. The rev-B five-FET consolidation was PARTLY REVERSED by BLOCKING-04 - recorded, not hidden.

J200/J300: CJT A3963WV-6P (VH-series-compatible, 10 A / 250 V) and A2541WV-4P, both -40..+105 C, rather than genuine JST VH/XH at -25..+85 C. Closes power_tree s10.5's housing question outright - no derating exception needed.

open_items.severity: P10 COST ITEM - compounds across the fixture
open_items.item: MANUAL ASSEMBLY IS NOT A FOOTNOTE ON THIS BOARD AND IT MUST BE COUNTED AT P10. J3 and J4 are REVERSE-MOUNTED THT sockets on the BOTTOM side (the ICD requires them to face down) and the bank is FOUR RADIAL THT electrolytics on the top. Neither is a standard JLC top-side SMD PCBA line. requirements s7 / open question 6 default (a) hand-finishes them locally at this quantity, which is viable for 4-6 boards but is real labour: 2 reverse-mounted sockets + 4 radial cans + the J200/J300 wire-to-board headers = 8 hand-soldered parts per daughter, plus the harness crimping. ORDER_QUOTE AT P10 MUST NOT ASSUME JLC FITS ANY OF THEM. AND IT COMPOUNDS: the carrier is separately accumulating a hand-fitted magjack, so the manual step count belongs in ONE place at P10 for the whole fixture, not per-board where it looks small twice.

R2 / ID_ADC board-type code. Was a 4.7k placeholder pending a carrier-owner allocation. ICD-01 s3.4 (rev A3) is now NORMATIVE and allocates LUM-STR-A code 1 = 2.7 kOhm 1%. Fixed in this revision. NOTE FOR WHOEVER CITES THE ICD NEXT: the document header still reads 'frozen at H1. Rev A3' while its own parenthetical lists amendments through A6 - cite the section and its amendment revision, not the header.

TWO HYSTERESIS VALUES COULD NOT BE RETARGETED TO THE BASIC SHELF WITHOUT MOVING A BAND MATERIALLY, so they are flagged rather than taken: U400C UVLO 820k (only Basic option is 1M, band -17.9 %, Vio margin 3.9x -> 3.2x on the band the architecture already calls the tightest) and U400D ceiling 620k (only Basic option is 510k, band +21.3 % = 0.31 V more of the 8.3 V window consumed). Full arithmetic in hysteresis_retargeting_report. Accepting both would take the network to zero Extended lines and save ~$1.00/board.

NO P-CHANNEL MOSFET IN THE JLC CATALOGUE CHARACTERISES SOA AT THE 590 ms COLD START. Verified against the datasheet, not the attribute strings: IRF5210S Fig 8 plots exactly three single-pulse lines - 100 usec, 1 msec, 10 msec - annotated 'Tc = 25 C, Tj = 150 C, Single Pulse'. Tc-REFERENCED, and NO DC LINE at all. IRF9540NS publishes the identical set. The 590 ms event is 59x beyond the longest plotted curve, in the un-characterised 10 ms-to-DC gap blocks.md s8 already names. Not a reason to reject the part (no alternative closes it); a reason the cold start must be justified by derivation from Zth and recorded in DOC-01. RthJC 0.75 C/W max, RthJA 40 C/W max with footnote (5) 'when mounted on 1 inch square PCB (FR-4 or G-10)' = 645 mm2 - exactly the check_thermal a_eff clamp. SECOND POINT: Q100's Tjmax is 150 C, NOT the pass FETs' 175 C. At the 90 C risk ambient the cold-start rise of 22-39 C puts Tj at 112-129 C against 150 C.

open_items.severity: documented derating exception - EXPECTED TO CLEAR
open_items.item: U420 MCP23008T-E/SS: the -E order code does mean -40..+125 C, but every DC and AC table is conditioned on E-Temp = Vdd 4.5-5.5 V. At this board's +3V3 the part is specified only to +85 C - the same ceiling as the TCA9534 it displaced, so the rationale for paying +$1.14 was void. Abs max ambient under bias remains +125 C, so the gap is UNSPECIFIED, NOT DESTRUCTIVE. UPDATE: the ICD s7.6 dispute resolved as an UNSTATED ASSUMPTION, not an arithmetic error - 56 C was the LED-heat-stays-in-the-box case, and the owner has closed the enclosure as sealed with the LED heatsink bolted THROUGH the wall, putting only ~1.9 W into the box (~32-33 C at a 25 C room). ICD s7.7 rev A5 is normative and holds internal air to 70 C. A +85 C specification ceiling clears 70 C, so this exception is expected to close - the architect is confirming against the re-issued section. Also recorded: the 3.3 V I2C ceiling is 400 kHz (1.7 MHz needs 4.5-5.5 V), which is fine - ICD s3.3 specifies 400 kHz.

open_items.severity: documented derating exception - EXPECTED TO CLEAR
open_items.item: U201..U351 SN74LVC1G3157DCKR (UMW): my earlier '-55..+125 C' came from an LCSC ATTRIBUTE STRING, not the datasheet. The PDF says -40 to +125 C, and every electrical table is characterised only over -40..+85 C - the same ceiling as the SGM3157 it replaced. Clears against ICD s7.7's 70 C for the same reason as P3-OPEN-8.

FLOATING-RAIL BIAS BUDGET. The 24k dropper delivers (48-12)/24k = 1.5 mA at 48 V and 1.9 mA at 57 V. An LM2904B draws up to 1.2 mA, so as little as 0.3 mA may be left to hold D101 above its zener knee. Separately the 24k 0805 dissipates 84 mW at 57 V against a 125 mW rating = 67 %, the only part of the charge loop without comfortable power margin. Lowering the dropper fixes one and worsens the other.

C175263 (39R 2512) has the THINNEST STOCK ON THIS BOM at 841 pieces - still 70x the 12-piece need, so it clears the 5x floor, but it is the row to re-check before ordering. ROHM LTR100JZPF39R0 (C2088806) is the same 2 W / 1 % / 100 ppm spec at 3810 stock for 2.4x the price.

The 680uF/100V D18x25 bank is effectively SINGLE-VENDOR (Ymin). The 6-footprint / 4-populated layout is what buys the second source, and it only pays off at 470 uF where AISHI / SamYoung / Chengx / Lelon all stock a 7.5 mm-pitch part. So blocks.md s6.3 mitigation 1 (drop the two spare footprints for 400 mm2 of F.Cu) and 'keep the bank's second source' are THE SAME LEVER. P6 cannot spend it twice.

Remaining generic protect-sheet resistor quantities (22k and 47k 0603, 6 each) are ESTIMATES, as are the two 10k for the Q101 level shift and the one 100nF for the charge-loop compensation. The rev-D network pinned about twenty previously-generic placements, which is why the pool shrank from 8+8 to 6+6. All are JLC Basic, so any E24 0603/0805 1% value P4 needs adds no feeder fee - only the placement count moves.

The hot-swap controller's fault timer versus the 87 %-duty current-limit regime (TPS2490 25/2.5 uA = 9.09 % break-even; LM5069 85/2.5 uA = 2.86 %). Accepted as BLOCKING-04; the controller is deleted and the limiter is a discrete linear loop with no timer.

P-CHANNEL IS NOT NEGOTIABLE - an N-channel high-side switch needs its gate above the 48 V rail, i.e. the charge pump the deleted controller provided internally. LINEAR-MODE EVIDENCE, read off the datasheet (Infineon/IR PD-97049B) rather than the LCSC attributes: Fig 8 'Maximum Safe Operating Area' plots only THREE single-pulse lines - 100 usec, 1 msec, 10 msec - annotated 'Tc = 25 C, Tj = 150 C, Single Pulse'. IT IS Tc-REFERENCED, AND THERE IS NO DC LINE AT ALL. The 590 ms cold start is 59x beyond the longest plotted curve, so it lands squarely in the un-characterised gap between the 10 ms line and DC - the same dead zone blocks.md s8 and power_tree s5.2 already name for every JLC-stocked MOSFET. NO PART IN THIS CATALOGUE CLOSES THAT GAP FROM PAPER; the cold start must be justified by derivation from Zth as power_tree s10.3 does, and recorded in DOC-01. THERMAL: RthJC 0.75 C/W max; RthJA 40 C/W max, footnote (5) 'when mounted on 1 inch square PCB (FR-4 or G-10)' = 645 mm2, which is exactly the check_thermal a_eff clamp - so the datasheet's own copper assumption and the P8 gate's agree. PD 170 W at Tc=25 C / 3.1 W at Ta=25 C, derating 1.3 W/C. Tj -55..+150 C. DUTY HERE: 0.215 W steady (11 C rise on the board's 51.1 C/W model) plus 2.56 J over 590 ms at cold start (mean 4.34 W; at Zth_JA(0.6 s) = 5-9 C/W that is a 22-39 C rise, so Tj = 112-129 C at the 90 C risk ambient against a 150 C Tjmax). NOTE Tjmax IS 150 C HERE, NOT the pass FETs' 175 C - the cold-start headroom is thinner than for an IRF640NS and should be stated in DOC-01. Chosen over IRF9540NS on die area at the same price: RthJC 0.75 vs 1.1 C/W, PD 170 vs 110 W, -38 A vs -23 A, and 3.7x the stock. Both publish the identical 100us/1ms/10ms curve set.

parts.role: R100/R101 series ballast, 2 x 39R in parallel = 19.5 ohm. THIS IS ALSO THE CURRENT-SENSE ELEMENT: at the 0.20 A limit it develops 3.9 V, which the LM2904B half senses directly - no shunt, no high-side sense amplifier, no precision reference. TOLERANCE IS LOAD-BEARING, not a formality: it sets the current limit directly as I = Vref/R, so +-1% is specified (this part) and a 5% part would smear the limit +-5% across the 0.172-0.220 A window. +-100 ppm/C adds only 0.35% over a 35 K swing. WORKING VOLTAGE 200 V: each part sees just 3.9 V in normal operation, but a loop failure with the FET fully on into an empty bank would put the full 48 V (57 V worst case) across the pair, so the 200 V rating is what makes that fault a thermal event rather than a flashover. POWER 0.303 W each steady (0.39 W each at the 0.20 A limit) against 2 W derated to 1.53 W at 90 C = 5.1x. Same Ever Ohms CRH2512 family as the 470R active bleed, so one vendor qualification covers both. STOCK IS THE THINNEST ON THIS BOM at 841 (70x the 12-piece need) - see alternates.

P4 MUST CHECK THE FLOATING-RAIL BIAS BUDGET: the 24k dropper delivers only (48-12)/24k = 1.5 mA (1.9 mA at 57 V), and an LM2904B draws up to 1.2 mA, so as little as 0.3 mA may be left to hold the zener above its knee. If the loop needs more headroom the dropper must come down from 24k, which costs dissipation on a 0805.

It only ever sees the 12 V across the floating rail, not the 48 V, so a 50 V part is legal. SECOND PLACEMENT AT REV D: blocks.md s2.4.3 specifies one shared 1 uF alongside the per-pin 100 nF for the two quad comparators, and records that the LM2901 datasheet publishes no decoupling guidance at all - so it is a design decision the architecture owns, not an omission. JLC Basic.
